title: An Ubuntu-Guided Large Language Model Framework for Cognitive Behavioral Mental Health Dialogue

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating fine-tuned model responses to expert-designed African mental health case studies using manual analysis to assess the integration of the African Ubuntu philosophy (Connectedness, Competency, Consciousness) and culturally adapted Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) techniques.

Manual evaluation of the model's linguistic expression to determine its alignment with South African communication norms, specifically examining the use of simplified English, familiar local names, respectful titles, African proverbs, and somatic descriptions of distress instead of Western clinical terminology.

Assessing the model's ability to provide context-appropriate spiritual support (e.g., integrating Christian scripture and guided prayer) in its dialogue, contrasting with predominantly secular Western psychological frameworks, evaluated through expert review of simulated conversations.
